openTomorrow: Yeah, definitely. I just set up this challenge with my friends and I want to track how we're doing. Plus, it's motivating to see the progress and check in with them.
secured: I think it means like, your data is protected and private? Or maybe it means you've locked in your commitment to the challenge so you can't back out easily.
freeze: I'm not totally sure, but I'm guessing it's like pausing your challenge temporarily if life gets crazy. Like you can freeze it instead of failing or quitting completely.
selfReported: That's where you log your own stuff manually instead of the app tracking it automatically. Like when I typed in 'Gym before worknnnnn' - I'm the one saying I did it, the app trusts me.
best: Honestly, the part where I finished setting up the challenge and saw it all come together. It feels legit now and I'm pumped to get my friends involved and actually do this.
worst: The typo in my habit name lol. I wrote 'worknnnnn' and now I'm stuck with it. Should've proofread before confirming.
tellFriend: 100%. I'd be like 'Yo, I found this app called GRIIT where we can make challenges together and track them. It's pretty sick - we should do a group one. I'm thinking fitness-focused but we could do anything.' My boys would probably be down.
